name: Henry Ford
role: Founder of the Ford Motor Company; industrialist and publisher of the Dearborn Independent
summary: Henry Ford built the Ford Motor Company on mass production, high wages and the 'service before profit' idea, opposed unions until 1941, and distrusted bankers, governments and war. He owned and sponsored a newspaper that ran a long antisemitic series based on the Protocols, which he later disowned.

public-ownership.rationale: He wrote that governments can promise something for nothing but cannot deliver, that help does not come from Washington but from ourselves, and favoured less government in business.

unions-good.rationale: His company refused to recognise the UAW, its Service Department attacked union organisers at the Rouge plant in 1937, and Ford was the last major automaker to recognise the union, in 1941, after a strike, according to The Henry Ford.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He wrote that laws can do very little, that law never does anything constructive and can never be more than a policeman, and that looking to legislation to abolish special privilege makes it grow.

traditional-family.rationale: He wrote that the division of labour in which the husband is bread-winner and the wife home-maker is the normal condition that will remain, while welcoming single women's self-support.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He wrote that it will be impossible to make the American people turn their faces like flint against those who wish to come, that America has been the open door and sanctuary, though not all modern immigrants are of pioneer quality.

free-trade.rationale: He wrote that foreign trade is full of delusions, that business rivalry between nations had a great deal to do with the war, and that every nation should be wished as large a degree of self-support as possible.

nation-first.rationale: He wrote that patriotism is an inclusive emotion and that America's heightened regard for the rights of all peoples is an internationalism of sympathy and understanding and good wishes.

central-planning.rationale: He wrote that Bolshevism blocked production in Russia and that regimenting people as to food, clothing and shelter does not make an economic system work, while the present order, though clumsy, works.

natural-rulers.rationale: He wrote that men of larger ability give leadership to the community and enable the smaller men to live with less effort, and that levelling them down harms all.

war-builds-character.rationale: He wrote that he was more opposed to war than ever, that war never settles anything, and that no patriot makes money out of war.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He called the idea of classes largely fictional, rejected the philosophy that progress consists in fomenting discord in industry, and said the union of those whose interests are interdependent is coming.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He wrote that the conception of democracy that names a levelling-down of ability makes for waste, since no two things in nature are alike and larger men give leadership to the community.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He said that instead of empty forms of government we need facts and the things to be done, and that experiments should settle questions by well-founded trial.

production-for-use.rationale: He listed putting service before profit as a principle, saying profit must be the result of service and not the basis of business, while holding there is nothing wrong in making a profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He wrote that Bolshevism blocked production and ruthlessly drove out skilled men, that the reformers wrecked Russia, and that it cannot work.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He wrote that business relations between nations had a great deal to do with the outbreak of the war, which was figured in advance on a profit basis, and that business had more to do with it than politics.

state-as-business.rationale: He wrote that 'less government in business and more business in government' is a very good slogan, that Americans may help the Government but the Government cannot help them, and that business principles should govern.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He wrote that the world owes nobody a living, that people were coddled into expecting social service, and that work should be found for even the disabled rather than relying on charity.

class-collaboration.rationale: He wrote that the doctrine of the class war is fallacious, that there are no fixed classes but only men who will work and men who will not, and that producers from drawing board to moulding floor should work together.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: His company set up the Ford English School and a Sociological Department to Americanize immigrant workers, who were expected to adopt the code of conduct and living set by the company, according to The Henry Ford.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He wrote that politics has become a professional matter in which party leaders with personal aspirations pre-select programmes and candidates and refuse to consider the people's thought, though the people hold political power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He wrote that law can never be more than a policeman and that it is a waste of time to look to state capitals or Washington to do what law was not designed to do.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He wrote that the doctrine of the Declaration is that men are equally endowed with fundamental rights, not equal qualities, and that the most inferior individual has rights which even the most superior dare not violate.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He wrote that the Government is only a committee of citizens selected to look after public affairs, that underneath the Constitution is the great mass of Americans, and that the people are the depository of political power.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: He called the modern city the most unlovely and unwholesome condition, concentrating all that is wrong, artificial and unjust in social life, and urged an exodus from the cities to the land.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: His Sociological Department investigated workers' home lives, savings and children's schooling and made the five-dollar wage depend on living as the company judged worthy, according to The Henry Ford.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He wrote that the Constitution is a social contract written on the hearts of the people, that no instrument is nearer perfect, and that the Government's affairs are all set forth in it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He owned and sponsored the Dearborn Independent, which carried 'Mr. Ford's Own Page' and from May 1920 ran the front-page series 'The International Jew' built on the forged Protocols of the Elders of Zion, distributed through Ford dealers, according to The Henry Ford and the American Jewish Archives.

local-production.rationale: He urged cultivating one's own market, wishing every nation to learn to supply itself with what it imports and to develop its own natural resources rather than depend on foreign trade.

religious-nation.rationale: He wrote that the genius of the United States is Christian in the broadest sense and its destiny is to remain Christian, without sectarian meaning.

family-wage.rationale: He wrote that there is something sacred about wages, which are homes and families, bread boxes, babies' cradles and children's education, and that the best wages yet paid are not as high as they ought to be.

collective-bargaining.rationale: His company refused to recognise the UAW until a ten-day strike in 1941, making it the last major automaker to sign a union contract, according to The Henry Ford.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: His company founded the Ford English School in 1914 to teach foreign-born employees to read, write and speak English, growing to more than 2,200 students by 1916, according to The Henry Ford.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: He said America's tradition is to be a refuge, but that not all modern immigrants are of pioneer quality and that immigrants who come to help make the country are welcome while those bringing destructive ideas and seeking to change the United States are not fit to be citizens.

notes: First audit. Read in full by search: My Life and Work (1922), Moving Forward (1931) and Today and Tomorrow (1926), searched by theme; his record is cited from reports by The Henry Ford and the American Jewish Archives (Dearborn Independent, five-dollar day, Sociological Department, 1937 and 1941 union conflict). The 1922 selection of 'Mr. Ford's Page' (Ford Ideals) is treated as his words because it was published as his ideas under his name, although Cameron wrote it. His 1927 signed retraction of the charges against Jews is cited as words and does not change the record of the paper he owned and sponsored from 1920. On the League of Nations: Wilson backed him for the Senate in 1918, but no statement of his own on it was found for 1918; in 1922 he called the League an ideal that is real, and in 1926 he called it controlled by financiers; neither settles whether it should have powers to enforce its decisions, so empower-international-orgs is null. Not searched: New York Times and Literary Digest interviews.
